Class LimitKeyRegistry

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.limit.LimitKeyRegistry
public abstract class LimitKeyRegistry extends Object
The catalogue of limit keys. It replaces the three static registries the limit configuration used to be spread over: Globalparameters.defaultLimitMap, TenantLimitsHelper.GLOBAL_LIMIT_KEY_TO_ENTITY_MAP and UserEntityChangeLimit.ADDITIONAL_LIMIT_ENTITY_NAMES.

The key space has two halves, because the two limit families need different things.

LimitType.MAX keys are registered explicitly. A counter, a parent relation, two scopes and a message key cannot be derived from an entity name, so an application registers each of them at startup. Saving a row against an unregistered MAX key is rejected.

LimitType.DAY_CUD and LimitType.DAY_READ keys are derived, not registered. Their counter is always user_entity_change_count and they have neither relation nor scopes, so the only thing to validate is the entity name. The valid set is every concrete, non-abstract BaseID entity that is neither tenant-owned nor an AdminEntity, taken from the JPA metamodel, plus the pseudo names registered here. This matches the generic daily-check path and lets a per-user row target an entity that has no configured default at all.

Registration happens once at startup from the application layer, so that grafiosch-base and grafiosch-server-base name no application class.

    • registerCudPseudoEntityName

      public static void registerCudPseudoEntityName(String entityName, Class<?> backingEntityClass)
      Registers a pseudo entity name that has no JPA entity but may carry a daily CUD limit, so the admin picker offers it.
      Parameters:

      backingEntityClass - the entity whose rows the name stands for, for example Security. It decides whether the administration UI shows the name as private or as shared data

    • isSharedData

      public static boolean isSharedData(Class<?> entityClass)
      Says whether an entity holds data shared between all tenants or data private to one client or one user. The administration UI shows this per row, because the limit key itself only carries it for the MAX family, in OwnerScope; the daily families have no scope at all.

      The test is deliberately negative. Being Auditable is not what makes data shared: Historyquote and Securitysplit extend plain BaseID and are shared data all the same. What marks data as not shared is that it belongs to exactly one owner, which is what TenantBaseID and UserBaseID express.

      Parameters:
      entityClass - the entity behind a limit key
      Returns:
      true when the entity holds shared data, false when it belongs to one client or one user

    • findFlatMaxForEntity

      public static Optional<LimitKeyRegistration> findFlatMaxForEntity(Class<?> entityClass)
      Finds the lifetime cap the generic REST create path enforces for an entity.

      Three kinds of registration are excluded. Keys guarding a nested collection, because their entity class is the parent and only the explicit call site knows the parent id. Keys under a pseudo entity name such as SimulationTenant, which count a subset of a table and would otherwise fire on every ordinary create of that table. And keys whose LimitKeyRegistration.checkedOnGenericCreate() is false, which already have a hand-written call site with a more specific error.

      Matching is by assignability rather than class identity, and the most specific registration wins. That is what makes a Securitycashaccount count against the Cashaccount cap, which class identity did not.

      Parameters:
      entityClass - the class of the entity about to be created
      Returns:
      the registration guarding it, or empty when the generic path enforces no cap for this entity
